question: Emphyteusis is a legal institution that exists in a number of Italian regions such as Apulia, Sicily and Sardinia, as well as in other EU Member States, including Malta, and Catalonia in Spain. Historically, emphyteusis served as a means of encouraging agricultural development. It obliges the lessee to improve the land they lease and to pay rent to the owner/grantor.

However, in many areas such as the Italian municipality of San Michele Salentino, citizens are bound by outdated contracts, with owners’/grantors’ heirs requiring lessees to pay excessive amounts in rent and arrears, giving rise to legal uncertainty and disputes.

These practices could be in breach of EU law, in particular the right to property (Article 17 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights) and the principle of proportionality, in addition to hindering the free movement of capital. In view of the above: 1.
Can the Commission clarify whether emphyteusis, as implemented in Italy and other Member States, is compatible with EU principles?
Will it take steps to protect the fundamental rights of citizens by ensuring that emphyteusis does not lead to abuse or disproportionate burdens?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.2.2025) Article 17 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union (the Charter) provides that everyone has the right to own, use, dispose of and bequeath his or her lawfully acquired possessions. However, according to its Article 51(1), the provisions of the Charter are addressed to the Member States only when they are implementing EU law.

On the basis of the information provided, it does not appear that the matter referred to by the Honourable Member is related to the implementation of EU law. In particular, there is nothing that indicates that the free movement of capital applies in the case at issue.

In the present case, it is thus for the concerned Member States to ensure that fundamental rights are effectively respected and protected in accordance with their national law and international obligations.
